correctness.rationale: Energy coercivity and strictly negative velocity dissipation give global attraction. A smooth odd center graph has exact cubic/quintic coefficients \(A=-c/a,\ B=-d/a+bc/a^2-3c^2/a^3\), derived from the invariance equation and rechecked symbolically. The deviation from this graph obeys an exact uniformly damped scalar equation, yielding exponential tracking of a center trajectory and the codimension-one fast exception. For every nonzero tracked center orbit, \(u=z^{-2}\) satisfies \(\dot u=2c/a-2B/u+O(u^{-2})\), whose integrable remainder yields a true constant C. An exact polynomial cofactor identity checks the cancellation iff. SymPy checker returned CHECK_OK; ODE integrations for coefficient signs agree. Neither numerical tests nor a CAS were used to replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2023 global-stability theorem gives no quantified algebraic or logarithmic relaxation. The 2017/2018 fast--slow literature treats power-order rates with velocity damping, while the 2021 polynomial Liénard integrability literature covers invariant polynomial curves and is credited for that subclaim. The new universal three-contribution logarithmic coefficient, full slow-versus-fast global classification for position damping, and iff zero-log transition are not stated or implied by the inspected works; the recorded mathematical literature searches found analogous normal-form logarithms in other systems, not the claimed Liénard family. Closest mathematical research record on a five-dimensional Lorenz model uses a similar scalar mechanism but cannot specialize to this scalar oscillator. This is a bounded self-review, not proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The full publisher article DOI 10.1016/j.geomphys.2021.104215 could not be retrieved; its indexed scientific text and the stronger related public full arXiv treat integrability rather than quantified two-term decay.

Analogous logarithmic drift formulas in unrelated center-manifold models use the same general normal-form method. Exact global novelty beyond the compared literature remains subject to independent expert review.

value.rationale: The nonhyperbolic, globally attracting Liénard family has a natural critical relaxation timescale; its leading inverse-square slope alone cannot distinguish how quintic stiffness, nonlinear damping and inertia bias finite-time recovery. The theorem gives the exact signed first logarithmic correction for all nonexceptional initial data, includes a measure-zero exponential fast set, and identifies precisely the codimension-one cancellation where the slow cubic manifold is algebraically exact. It thus explains a real parameter-dependent change in threshold-time asymptotics rather than a routine reparameterization or arbitrary numerical slice. The special algebraic curve is not counted as independently new.
